title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues the previous page (54), which set up a fundamental group based at a 1-connected T. For a 1-connected (simply connected, possibly pro-) scheme T over X, E^T_X denotes the fundamental group (or Galois/étale fundamental group) of X with base T. The fibre functor is X' ↦ Hom_X(T, X'), which is a fibre functor because every finite étale cover of T splits. For a morphism X → Y and T → X, the previous page set E^T_{X/Y} := Ker(E^T_X → E^T_Y) and stated (11) that it is functorial in the triple (T → X → Y). Special cases there were geometric points, universal covers X̃, and Y = Spec A.

This page starts from a map T → Y with a lift T → X. Equivalently this is a section T → X_T of the base change X_T = X ×_Y T → T; the cartesian square X ← X_T, Y ← T is drawn with the diagonal section T → X_T.

Under the hypothesis that the 'homotopy exact sequence' holds, Grothendieck asserts two things.
- (12) E^T_{X/Y} ≅ π_1(X_T; T) ≅ E^T_{X_T}: the relative fundamental group is the fundamental group of the 'fibre' X_T over the simply connected base T, based at the given section.
- (13) There is a short exact sequence 1 → E^T_{X/Y} → E^T_X → E^T_Y → 1.

He notes this holds when Y = Spec K is a field and X is geometrically connected over K. This is the fundamental exact sequence 1 → π_1(X_{K̄}) → π_1(X) → G_K → 1.

He then starts the case where a 'universal homotopy exact sequence' holds but E_X → E_Y is not surjective. Page 55 handles it by a canonical factorization X → Y' → Y with Y' finite (or pro-finite) étale over Y. This is a Stein-type / relative π_0 factorization, after which E_X → E_{Y'} is onto and E_{X/Y} ≅ E_{X/Y'}.

Purpose: in the Longue Marche context, to have a base-point-flexible and functorial 'relative fundamental group' and its exact sequence. The previous page says the real goal is a 'universal homotopy exact sequence' in dimension 2, so that extension classes / outer actions attached to X → Y with 1-connected T can be interpreted via relative fundamental groups (anabelian set-up for families, e.g. curves over arithmetic bases).
errors: (12) cannot hold for an arbitrary 1-connected T without a strong 'universal' hypothesis. Take Y = Spec K of characteristic p, X = A^1_K and T = Spec Ω with Ω a separably closed field strictly larger than K^s. Then E^T_{X/Y} = π_1(X_{K^s}), whereas π_1(X_Ω) is strictly bigger (wild Artin–Schreier covers). So π_1(X_T) ≅ E_{X/Y} fails for non-proper X in positive characteristic.

The isomorphism holds for T = the universal (pro-)cover Ỹ, e.g. Spec K^s. It holds for general simply connected T only if 'suite exacte d'homotopie' is understood as stable under arbitrary 1-connected base change, which is presumably the meaning of the 'universelle' qualifier introduced at the end of the page.

The parenthetical 'always satisfied if Y = Spec K and X geometrically connected' needs X quasi-compact and quasi-separated (SGA1 IX 6.1). It is only valid with T = Spec K^s, or with X proper / characteristic 0, if T may be a larger separably closed field.

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at a simply connected scheme T → X instead of a geometric point; fibre functor X' ↦ Hom_X(T, X')
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group with pro-object / simply connected base point (generalized base points, cf. tangential base points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1, fibre functors); Deligne for tangential base points (1989)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 V (fibre functors in general Galois categories); Esquisse d'un programme mentions tangential base points

ideas.what: Relative fundamental group E^T_{X/Y} = Ker(E^T_X → E^T_Y) identified with π_1 of the base-changed fibre X_T at the section
ideas.modern_name: geometric fundamental group / kernel in the homotopy exact sequence

ideas.what: Short exact sequence 1 → π_1(X_{K̄}) → π_1(X) → G_K → 1 for X geometrically connected over K
ideas.modern_name: fundamental exact sequence of étale fundamental groups
ideas.where_published: SGA1 IX 6.1; La Longue Marche; Esquisse

ideas.what: When E_X → E_Y is not surjective, factor X → Y' → Y with Y' (pro-)finite étale over Y so that E_X → E_{Y'} becomes surjective (continued on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Stein factorization / relative π_0 (étale part of Stein factorization)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working-out of the SGA1 homotopy exact sequence in Grothendieck's own notation, with a 1-connected T as base point. Everything is standard. The only noteworthy point is the somewhat careless generality of T, which overreaches in characteristic p.
transcription_corrections: 'Ceci posé, [?]' — the image reads 'Ceci posé;'. The marginal text to the right of the diagram reads roughly 'on aura une iso-[morphisme] ... (sous l'hypo-thèse "suite exacte d'homotopie" satisfaite)'.
In the diagram the diagonal arrow goes from T (bottom right) to X_T: it is the section T → X_T, not an unlabeled '↖'.
'et on a [?]' before (13) — the image reads 'et on aura'.
'(cette hypothèse est [?] toujours satisfaite' — the image reads '(Cette hypothèse est satisfaite si Y = Spec K, K un corps, si X est géom. connexe sur K)'.
Last line: 'mais pas nécessairement E^T_X → E^T_Y surj,' — consistent with the image.
